title: KMT Government Retreats to Taiwan
verification_source: Wikipedia: Retreat of the government of the Republic of China to Taiwan — Chiang Kai-shek fled to Taiwan in 1949 with roughly 1–2 million military and civilians (figure varies by source; ~1.2M is within the cited range).

title: White Terror Begins Under Martial Law
verification_source: Wikipedia: Martial law in Taiwan — declared 19 May 1949, lifted 15 July 1987, lasting 38 years and 56–57 days (longest in modern history).

title: Korean War Saves Taiwan: US 7th Fleet Deployed
verification_source: Multiple sources confirm Truman ordered the 7th Fleet into the Taiwan Strait after North Korea invaded South Korea in June 1950, blocking a planned PRC invasion.

title: US Military Aid and Economic Assistance Begins
verification_source: Well-documented Cold War history: US Military Assistance Advisory Group dispatched and economic aid resumed following Korean War outbreak.

title: Land Reform Transforms Rural Economy
verification_source: Wikipedia: Land reform in Taiwan — Land-to-the-Tiller Act enacted May 1952, implemented through 1953. The event year 1952 is defensible as the legislative completion date.

title: US-ROC Mutual Defense Treaty Signed
verification_source: Avalon Project / Wikipedia: Treaty signed December 2, 1954 in Washington D.C., remained in force until 1979.

title: First Taiwan Strait Crisis: PRC Bombards Quemoy
verification_source: Wikipedia: First Taiwan Strait Crisis — PRC bombardment began September 3, 1954; Formosa Resolution passed January 29, 1955; shelling ceased May 1, 1955.

title: Second Taiwan Strait Crisis: Massive PRC Artillery Barrage
verification_source: Wikipedia / RAND: Bombardment began August 23, 1958; ~470,000–500,000 shells fired; alternate-day shelling continued until 1979.

title: Lei Chen Arrested, Free China Movement Suppressed
verification_source: Wikipedia: Lei Chen — arrested September 4, 1960; sentenced to 10 years on charges of harboring a communist; released 1970.

title: US Economic Aid Program Ends: Taiwan Graduates
verification_source: Well-documented: USAID formally terminated Taiwan program in 1965 as Taiwan had become a middle-income economy.

title: Export Processing Zones Established at Kaohsiung
verification_source: EPZA / Taiwan Panorama: First EPZ established December 3, 1966 at Kaohsiung — the world's first export processing zone.

title: ROC Expelled from United Nations; PRC Takes Seat
verification_source: Wikipedia: UN General Assembly Resolution 2758, adopted October 25, 1971 by 76–35 vote; PRC took China's UN seat.

title: Nixon-Mao Shanghai Communique Undermines Taiwan
verification_source: Wikipedia: Shanghai Communiqué issued February 27, 1972; US 'acknowledged' one China position without explicitly endorsing it.

title: Ten Major Construction Projects Launch Industrial Scale-Up
verification_source: Wikipedia: Ten Major Construction Projects — announced November 1973 by Premier Chiang Ching-kuo; included nuclear plants, steel mills, petrochemical plants, freeway.

title: Chiang Kai-shek Dies After 26 Years in Power
verification_source: Wikipedia: Chiang Kai-shek died April 5, 1975 in Taipei; succeeded by Vice President Yen Chia-kan.

title: Chiang Ching-kuo Elected President
verification_source: Wikipedia: Chiang Ching-kuo elected president by National Assembly in 1978.

title: US Derecognizes Taiwan, Establishes Relations with PRC
verification_source: Wikipedia / Heritage Foundation: Carter announced derecognition December 15, 1978; took effect January 1, 1979; Mutual Defense Treaty terminated one year later.

title: Taiwan Relations Act Passes US Congress
verification_source: Congress.gov: TRA signed by Carter April 10, 1979; established AIT as de facto embassy; provided for defensive arms sales.

title: Kaohsiung Incident: Democracy Movement Watershed
verification_source: Wikipedia: Kaohsiung Incident — December 10, 1979; Formosa Magazine rally violently dispersed; Annette Lu and Huang Hsin-chieh among those arrested.

title: Lin Family Murders Shock Democratic Movement
verification_source: Wikipedia: Lin Yi-hsiung — February 28, 1980; wife and twin daughters (age 6) stabbed to death; eldest daughter survived; house was under police surveillance.

title: TSMC Founder Morris Chang Joins Industrial Technology Research Institute
verification_source: Wikipedia: Morris Chang — joined ITRI in 1985, not 1980. The event year (1980) contradicts both the description's own hedging and verified facts. Year off by 5.
notes: The description itself contains an internal contradiction, mentioning 1985 in the text while the event is dated 1980.

title: Henry Liu (Deng Nan-jung) Assassination in California
verification_source: Wikipedia: Henry Liu — shot October 15, 1984 in Daly City, California by Bamboo Union agents acting on orders from Taiwan's Military Intelligence Bureau (not Defense Intelligence Bureau as stated, but the error is minor).
notes: Description says 'Defense Intelligence Bureau'; correct body was the Military Intelligence Bureau (KMT). Minor label error but facts otherwise accurate.

title: Democratic Progressive Party Founded Illegally
verification_source: Wikipedia: DPP founded September 28, 1986 at Grand Hotel Taipei without government authorization; Chiang Ching-kuo chose not to prosecute.

title: Martial Law Lifted After 38 Years
verification_source: Wikipedia: Martial law lifted July 15, 1987 by Chiang Ching-kuo; duration 38 years and 56–57 days.

title: Taiwan Opens Cross-Strait Family Visits to Mainland
verification_source: Well-documented: following martial law lifting in 1987, Taiwan permitted mainlander veterans to visit relatives in China for the first time.

title: TSMC Founded: World's First Pure-Play Foundry
verification_source: Wikipedia: TSMC founded 1987 by Morris Chang as joint venture with Taiwan government and Philips; pioneered pure-play foundry model.

title: Lee Teng-hui Becomes First Taiwanese-Born President
verification_source: Wikipedia: Chiang Ching-kuo died January 13, 1988; Lee Teng-hui sworn in as first native Taiwanese-born president.

title: Press Law Revised, Newspapers Liberalized
verification_source: Historical record: Taiwan lifted ban on new newspaper licenses in 1989 as part of broader democratization.

title: ROC Formally Ends State of War with PRC
verification_source: Wikipedia: National Assembly terminated the Period of National Mobilization for Suppression of the Communist Rebellion in April 1991.

title: First Full Legislative Yuan Elections Held
verification_source: Wikipedia: 1992 Taiwan legislative election — held December 19, 1992; first fully competitive election for all LY seats; KMT won majority, DPP gained substantially.

title: 1992 Consensus on Cross-Strait Relations
verification_source: Well-documented diplomatic history: SEF-ARATS talks in 1992 produced the ambiguous 'one China, respective interpretations' framework.

title: Koo-Wang Talks: First Official Cross-Strait Negotiations
verification_source: Wikipedia: Koo-Wang talks — SEF Chairman Koo Chen-fu and ARATS Chairman Wang Daohan met in Singapore, April 1993; produced four agreements.

title: Taiwan Launches 'Go South' Economic Policy
verification_source: Well-documented: Taiwan introduced Southward Policy in 1994 to diversify investment toward Southeast Asia.

title: Lee Teng-hui Visits Cornell University
verification_source: Wikipedia: Lee Teng-hui visited Cornell University in June 1995; first sitting ROC president to visit US since 1978; triggered Third Taiwan Strait Crisis.

title: Third Taiwan Strait Crisis: PRC Missile Tests
verification_source: Wikipedia: PRC missile tests began July 1995, continuing into 1996; US deployed two carrier battle groups to region.

title: First Direct Presidential Election: Lee Teng-hui Wins
verification_source: Wikipedia: 1996 Taiwanese presidential election — March 23, 1996; Lee won 54% of vote amid ongoing PRC missile tests.

title: US Carrier Groups Deter PRC During Strait Crisis
verification_source: Wikipedia: USS Independence and USS Nimitz deployed to Taiwan Strait region in March 1996 during Third Taiwan Strait Crisis.

title: Taiwan Economy Weathers Asian Financial Crisis
verification_source: Historical record: Taiwan avoided IMF bailout during 1997–98 Asian financial crisis due to large forex reserves and limited short-term debt.

title: Major Earthquake Kills 2,400 in Central Taiwan
verification_source: Wikipedia: 1999 Jiji earthquake — September 21, 1999; Mw 7.6; 2,415 killed, 11,305 injured. Description says 'approximately 2,400' — accurate.

title: Lee Teng-hui's Two-States Theory Provokes Beijing
verification_source: Wikipedia: Lee Teng-hui's 'special state-to-state' statement made in radio interview July 1999; Beijing suspended cross-strait dialogue.

title: Chen Shui-bian Wins Presidency: First DPP Victory
verification_source: Wikipedia: 2000 Taiwanese presidential election — March 18, 2000; Chen won 39.3% in three-way race; KMT split between Lien Chan and James Soong.

title: Taiwan Joins World Trade Organization
verification_source: WTO official records: Taiwan acceded January 1, 2002, not January 2001. Year off by 1.

title: Chen Shui-bian's 'One Country on Each Side' Statement
verification_source: Wikipedia: Chen made the 'one country on each side' statement in August 2002; alarmed Washington and Beijing.

title: SARS Outbreak Hits Taiwan Hard
verification_source: CDC/NIH: Taiwan had 346 confirmed SARS-CoV(+) cases; 73 deaths; Hoping Hospital was the worst-affected cluster.

title: Chen Shui-bian Re-elected After Assassination Attempt
verification_source: Wikipedia: Chen was shot in the abdomen (stomach), not merely 'grazed'. Annette Lu was grazed in the knee. The description says both were 'grazed by bullets' — materially incorrect for Chen.
notes: Margin of ~25,563 votes is accurate; date (March 20, 2004) is accurate. The 'grazed' characterization for Chen is the material error.

title: China's Anti-Secession Law Threatens Force Against Taiwan
verification_source: Wikipedia: Anti-Secession Law enacted March 2005; first explicit legal trigger for military action against Taiwan.

title: Cross-Strait Charter Flights Begin for Lunar New Year
verification_source: Well-documented: First direct charter flights across strait during Lunar New Year 2005; first since 1949.

title: Chen Shui-bian Corruption Scandal Paralyzes Government
verification_source: Wikipedia: Wu Shu-jen (Chen's wife) charged with misusing state affairs fund; Shih Ming-teh led mass protests for Chen's resignation in 2006.

title: Ma Ying-jeou Wins Presidency: KMT Returns to Power
verification_source: Wikipedia: 2008 Taiwanese presidential election — Ma won 58% of vote; KMT also won legislative supermajority.

title: Direct Cross-Strait Flights, Shipping, and Mail Links Opened
verification_source: Wikipedia: 'Three links' implemented December 2008 after 60 years of separation.

title: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement Negotiations Begin
verification_source: Wikipedia: ECFA negotiations began 2009; signed June 2010.

title: ECFA Signed: Landmark Cross-Strait Trade Agreement
verification_source: Wikipedia: ECFA signed June 2010; reduced tariffs on hundreds of goods and services.

title: Ma Ying-jeou Re-elected, Cross-Strait Ties Continue
verification_source: Wikipedia: 2012 Taiwanese presidential election — Ma won January 2012 with 51% vs Tsai's 45%.

title: Cross-Strait Services Trade Agreement Signed
verification_source: Wikipedia: Cross-Strait Services Trade Agreement signed June 2013; secretive process fueled 2014 Sunflower Movement.

title: Sunflower Movement Occupies Legislature Against Services Pact
verification_source: Wikipedia: Sunflower Movement began March 18, 2014; occupation lasted 24 days until April 10; blocked services agreement.

title: Hong Kong Umbrella Movement Deepens Taiwan-China Divide
verification_source: Wikipedia: Umbrella Movement ran September–December 2014; failure strengthened Taiwanese skepticism of 'one country, two systems'.

title: Xi-Ma Summit in Singapore: First Cross-Strait Leader Meeting
verification_source: Wikipedia: Ma Ying-jeou and Xi Jinping met in Singapore on November 7, 2015; first meeting between leaders of both sides since 1949.

title: Tsai Ing-wen Elected: First Female President, DPP Majority
verification_source: Wikipedia: 2016 Taiwanese presidential election — January 16, 2016; Tsai won 56.1%; DPP won legislative majority.

title: Beijing Suspends Cross-Strait Dialogue After Tsai Election
verification_source: Wikipedia: China suspended SEF-ARATS mechanism after Tsai's election due to her refusal to endorse 1992 Consensus.

title: Taiwan Launches New Southbound Policy
verification_source: Well-documented: Tsai launched New Southbound Policy in 2016 to diversify toward Southeast/South Asia and Oceania.

title: Panama Breaks Ties with Taiwan, Recognizes PRC
verification_source: Wikipedia: Panama cut ties with Taiwan and established relations with PRC on June 13, 2017.

title: PLA Air Force Begins Regular Median Line Crossings
verification_source: Well-documented: PLA ADIZ incursions escalated markedly from 2018–2019 onward, with median line crossings becoming systematic.

title: Hong Kong's National Security Law Collapses 'One Country, Two Systems' Credibility
verification_source: Wikipedia: Hong Kong protests began June 2019; National Security Law imposed June 2020; boosted Tsai's re-election.
notes: The event is dated 2019 and covers the start of protests; NSL came in 2020 but the event accurately frames 2019 as when the credibility collapse began.

title: Taiwan Legalizes Same-Sex Marriage
verification_source: Wikipedia / Amnesty International: Bill passed May 17, 2019; signed May 22; took effect May 24, 2019 — first in Asia.

title: Tsai Ing-wen Re-elected in Landslide Amid Hong Kong Crisis
verification_source: Wikipedia: 2020 Taiwanese presidential election — January 11, 2020; Tsai won 8.17 million votes, 57.13%.

title: Taiwan's COVID-19 Response Wins International Praise
verification_source: Well-documented: Taiwan's early COVID-19 response in 2020 widely cited as among world's most effective; WHO exclusion issue confirmed.

title: Global Chip Shortage Elevates TSMC's Strategic Centrality
verification_source: Well-documented: 2020–2021 global semiconductor shortage exposed TSMC's centrality; triggered US/EU/Japan efforts to onshore capacity.

title: TSMC Begins Arizona Fabrication Plant Construction
verification_source: TSMC press release / Wikipedia: $12 billion fab announced May 2020, construction began 2021. Description correctly states '$12 billion' as original figure.

title: PLA Conducts Record Air Incursions into Taiwan ADIZ
verification_source: Wikipedia: PLA conducted record 56-aircraft single-day incursion in October 2021; hundreds of sorties throughout the year.

title: Pelosi Visit Triggers Unprecedented PLA Encirclement Drills
verification_source: Wikipedia: Pelosi visited August 2–3, 2022; PLA exercises ran August 4–11; 5 missiles landed in Japan's EEZ — confirmed.

title: US CHIPS and Science Act Incentivizes Taiwan Semiconductor Diversification
verification_source: Congress.gov: CHIPS and Science Act enacted August 2022; $52 billion in subsidies; restrictions on expanding advanced capacity in China.

title: Taiwan Loses More Diplomatic Allies to PRC
verification_source: Honduras switched in March 2023, not 2022. The event year 2022 is incorrect by 1 year.

title: Taiwan Defense Budget Hits Record as Military Threat Grows
verification_source: SCMP / CFR: Taiwan approved record defense budget of ~NT$606.8 billion (~$19 billion) for 2024, announced August 2023; conscription extended to one year.
notes: Description says NT$610 billion; official figure was NT$606.8 billion — minor rounding difference, not materially wrong.

title: William Lai Selected as DPP Presidential Candidate
verification_source: Wikipedia: William Lai won DPP primary in 2023; Beijing had labeled him a 'troublemaker'; geopolitical stakes elevated heading into 2024 election.

title: Lai Ching-te Wins Presidency; KMT Makes Legislative Gains
verification_source: Wikipedia: January 13, 2024; Lai won 40.05% in three-way race; DPP lost legislative majority; third consecutive DPP presidential win.

title: Major Earthquake Strikes Hualien, Killing Dozens
verification_source: Wikipedia: 2024 Hualien earthquake — April 3, 2024; Mw 7.4; at least 19 killed (not 'at least 13' as stated). Materially wrong death toll.

title: PRC Launches Military Drills After Lai Ching-te Inauguration
verification_source: Wikipedia: Joint Sword-2024A launched May 23, 2024, three days after Lai's inauguration; two-day encirclement exercise involving PLA Army, Navy, Air Force, Rocket Force, and Coast Guard.
